**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 23rd November 2010</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for August 2010** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for August 2010 world copper supply and demand in its November 2010 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for August 2010 indicated a production deficit of about 19,000 metric tonnes (t). When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, August showed a deficit of about 88,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first eight month of 2010, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 363,000 t (a seasonally adjusted deficit of 121,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of around 47,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of about 178,000 t) in the same period of 2009. 

During the first 8 months of 2010, world apparent usage grew by 8.3% (approximately 1 million tons) compared with that in same period of 2009 mainly owing to recovery from weak 2009 usage levels in the European Union (EU), Japan and the United States, where usage grew by 12.5%, 30% and 7.5%, respectively.  Although these year-on-year growth rates are strong, usage in the EU, Japan and United States was still well below pre-crisis levels (below Jan-Aug 2008 levels by 19%, 18% and 21% respectively).  In the first 8 months of 2010, Chinese apparent usage* increased by a more modest 4.5% from the very strong 2009 apparent usage level. 

In August, world mine production increased by almost 3% from that in August 2009, but cumulative production for the first 8 months of 2010 increased by only1% (114,000 t) compared with that in the first 8 months of 2009: concentrate and solvent extractionelectrowinning production both grew by about 1%. Production in Chile was up by 2% from its low level during the same period of 2009, but output from, Peru, the United States, Australia and Indonesia decreased by an aggregated 7.3% (213,000t).  These four countries represent around 25% of total world copper mine production.  The mine capacity utilization rate in the first eight month of 2010 (79.5%) was down slightly from the already low comparative rate in 2009 

During the first eight month of 2010, world refined production increased by 5.7% (680,000 t) compared with production in the same period of 2009: primary production increased by 2.3%, while secondary production (from scrap) increased by 25%. Note that the large relative increase in secondary refined copper production reflects in part the lower copper prices and consequent tight scrap market that existed in early 2009. World growth has been mainly driven by China (17%), Japan (9%) and the EU (9%),that combined represent almost one half of world refined copper production. Production in two other major world refiners, Chile and the United States, which account for about one quarter of

world production, decreased by a combined 2.3%. The refined production capacity utilization rate in the first eight month of 2010 increased to 79.6% from 76.6% in the same period of 2009 and reflects increased scrap availability and the restoration of temporary cuts made in early 2009. The average LME cash price for October 2010 was US$ 8,292.40 per tonne, up from the August 2010 average of US$ 7,709.30 per tonne. The 2010 high and low copper prices through the end of October were US$8,501.00 and US$6,091.00 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$7,281.04 per tonne. As of the end of October 2010, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 541,796 t, a decrease of 145,895 t from stocks held at the end of December 2009. Compared with the September levels, stocks were down at COMEX and LME but up at SHFE.
